name: jobhunt.resume
description: Jobhunt 0-10 quality bar for a resume, scored against a target lane or posting. state = the resume's extracted text, optionally followed by '=== TARGET ===' and the posting or target-lane brief. Scored on an 11-level scale where 0 is a defect, 5 is average and ignored, 10 is what good looks like. Goal: every question at 9.5 or above before submission.

a1_musthave_coverage.instructions: How completely the resume answers the target's stated must-have skills, tools and responsibilities in the target's own words
criteria: 0: fewer than half the must-haves appear at all
2: more than half appear; wording drifts from the target
3: all appear, but only in a keyword strip or skills block
4: all appear inside real bullets; one or two carry no proof
5: most must-haves in the target's words with evidence beside them
6: every must-have in the target's words; one bullet unsupported
7: every must-have backed by a dated bullet; numbers thin
8: every must-have backed by a dated, quantified outcome
9: 8's level and the target's own framing is echoed in the opener
10: every must-have restated in the target's words and answered with a dated, quantified outcome a reader can verify

a2_parseability.instructions: Whether a plain-text ATS extraction preserves all content with clean structure
criteria: 0: tables, text boxes or graphics destroy content
2: text survives but dates or order are mangled
3: parses, but core content sits in a table or multi-column block
4: single column, one non-standard heading name
5: clean single column and standard headings; one ambiguous date
6: standard headings, MM/YYYY throughout, contact block plain text
7: 6's level plus no empty paragraphs or orphan headings
8: 7's level plus consistent tense and punctuation in every bullet
9: 8's level plus a professional, versioned filename
10: 9's level plus extraction is byte-stable and the file hash is recorded

a3_chronology.instructions: How completely and consistently dates and gaps are handled
criteria: 0: contradictory dates or a gap an ATS flags as inconsistency
2: months missing on the current role
3: months missing on two or more roles
4: months present, one combined range left undeclared
5: exact months where forms need them; one combined range declared
6: no unexplained gap; any overlap between roles is explained
7: 6's level plus month precision matches the applications filed
8: 7's level plus every level change has its date
9: 8's level plus date format identical everywhere
10: 9's level plus chronology survives cross-check against the completed applications

a4_title_level_calibration.instructions: Whether titles stay verbatim and the framing matches the target's level and domain
criteria: 0: a title was altered, invented or inflated
2: framing reads a level above the target
3: framing is generic and level-neutral
4: opening line names the domain but not the level
5: titles verbatim and the level reads compatible with the target
6: titles verbatim and the opener names the target's domain
7: 6's level plus the opener names the class of problem owned
8: 7's level plus seniority is evidenced by scope, not adjectives
9: 8's level plus the target's own role wording appears once in the opener
10: 9's level plus the level calibration is consistent across every role block

a5_quantified_outcomes.instructions: How much of the experience is stated as a measurable outcome with a resolvable basis
criteria: 0: no numbers anywhere
2: one or two numbers in the whole document
3: numbers appear only in the summary
4: half the senior bullets carry a number
5: most senior bullets carry a number or named outcome
6: most bullets carry a number with scope (team, budget, region)
7: every senior bullet carries a number and scope
8: 7's level plus each number traces to an owner-verifiable source
9: 8's level plus outcomes are business results, not activity counts
10: 9's level plus every claim survives a sceptical read with no open question

b1_opening_answers_who.instructions: Whether the first three lines say who he is, at what level, and for what class of problem
criteria: 0: adjective-heavy leader language, no domain
2: names a domain but reads generic
3: names domain and level, no problem owned
4: names domain, level and one vague goal
5: names domain and level and the class of work
6: 5's level plus one evidence hook in the first block
7: 6's level plus the hook carries a number
8: 7's level plus the hook names the buyer's problem
9: 8's level plus it is two sentences or fewer
10: 9's level plus a recruiter could restate his pitch back after reading only these lines

b2_top_third_density.instructions: How much of the top third of page one maps to what the target wants
criteria: 0: the top third is a paragraph of adjectives
2: a quarter relevant
3: a third relevant
4: nearly half relevant
5: half the top-third lines map to a target requirement
6: more than half map to a target requirement
7: the top third is mostly target-relevant and the rest is trimmed
8: 7's level plus the highest-value evidence appears above the fold
9: 8's level plus nothing above the fold is filler
10: 9's level plus the top third alone would earn a full read

b3_scannability.instructions: Whether a skimming recruiter can absorb it in thirty seconds
criteria: 0: paragraphs past four lines or more than two pages
2: bullets present, most past four lines
3: bullets at three or four lines
4: bullets at two or three lines, uneven spacing
5: bullets mostly two lines with deliberate whitespace
6: 5's level plus scannable headings that match the target's vocabulary
7: 6's level plus the strongest bullet is first in each role
8: 7's level plus no redundant phrasing between bullets
9: 8's level plus one page for a ten-year scope is achievable without loss
10: 9's level plus a thirty-second read leaves a complete picture

b4_differentiation.instructions: How unmistakable he is against a generic AI leader resume
criteria: 0: interchangeable with any AI leadership resume
2: one unusual fact, unquantified
3: one distinctive proof, buried low
4: two distinctive proofs, both unquantified
5: one distinctive proof with a number in the top third
6: two distinctive proofs with numbers
7: 6's level plus one proof only he can claim (domain, scale or event)
8: 7's level plus the proofs are results, not job duties
9: 8's level plus the proofs name recognisable customers or entities
10: 9's level plus the differentiation is the spine of the whole document

b5_story_coherence.instructions: Whether the career reads as a deliberate progression with this role as the obvious next step
criteria: 0: the moves look unrelated and unexplained
2: one unexplained move or gap dominates
3: a pattern is visible but never stated
4: the pattern is stated in the summary only
5: the pattern is visible and the next step is credible
6: 5's level plus each move has a one-line reason
7: 6's level plus the most recent role clearly builds on the prior ones
8: 7's level plus the target role is the natural continuation
9: 8's level plus the summary states the trajectory in one clause
10: 9's level plus a sceptic would call the path intentional

c1_names_their_problem.instructions: How directly the resume answers the problem the target says it is hiring for
criteria: 0: only his own experience, no connection to their need
2: a plausible problem, not theirs
3: their domain's problem in his words
4: their problem approximated using their vocabulary
5: their problem named in their own words from the posting
6: 5's level plus one line of evidence against it
7: 6's level plus the evidence is a comparable win
8: 7's level plus two comparable wins at similar scope
9: 8's level plus the wins are in their sector or an adjacent regulated one
10: 9's level plus he addresses the hardest duty in the posting first

c2_same_class_of_outcome.instructions: Whether he has personally owned outcomes of the same scale and complexity the target implies
criteria: 0: only adjacent or smaller-scale work
2: one comparable example, scope unstated
3: one comparable example with scope stated
4: two comparable examples, one thin on scope
5: one comparable win with clear scope and a result
6: two comparable wins with scope and results
7: 6's level plus the complexity (ambiguity, stakeholders) is explicit
8: 7's level plus one win shows recovery or turnaround
9: 8's level plus the wins span strategy and execution, not one or the other
10: 9's level plus a hiring manager could hand him the same problem on day one

c3_scale_with_provenance.instructions: Whether team, budget, portfolio or executive scale is stated and can be backed
criteria: 0: no scale stated anywhere
2: scale claimed with no basis
3: one scale number with no basis
4: two scale numbers, basis vague
5: two scale numbers with a named basis
6: team and budget or portfolio both stated with basis
7: 6's level plus the executive audience is named
8: 7's level plus scope is stated per role, not once globally
9: 8's level plus every scale figure has an owner-verifiable source
10: 9's level plus the scale is unusual enough to be remembered

c4_execution_over_vocabulary.instructions: Whether he shows shipped work rather than strategy vocabulary
criteria: 0: buzzwords with no delivered artifact
2: one shipped artifact, unquantified
3: one shipped artifact with a date
4: two shipped artifacts, one vague
5: named shipped artifacts with dates and scope
6: 5's level plus the artifacts are systems or platforms, not slides
7: 6's level plus a named integration or adoption result
8: 7's level plus an operating cadence he established is named
9: 8's level plus he names what he built that outlived him
10: 9's level plus the delivery record is unmistakable in every role block

c5_bet_a_quarter_on_him.instructions: Whether the precision of the details signals reliability under load
criteria: 0: details sloppy or internally contradictory
2: consistent formatting but vague claims
3: clean and competent but unremarkable
4: clean, with one strong detail
5: competent, clean, with two strong specific details
6: 5's level plus numbers appear where a careful person would ask
7: 6's level plus no sentence raises a follow-up he cannot answer
8: 7's level plus the document demonstrates judgement (prioritisation, tradeoffs)
9: 8's level plus he names what he would not do as well as what he would
10: 9's level plus the reader would assume he is already operating at that level

d1_screen_questions_answerable.instructions: Whether the five questions a recruiter asks on a first screen can each be answered from the text alone
criteria: 0: most of the five cannot be answered from the text
2: two or three are answerable
3: three are answerable, one contradicts itself
4: four are answerable, one is thin
5: all five are answerable and mutually consistent
6: 5's level plus each answer is one sentence of evidence
7: 6's level plus the numbers match across every section
8: 7's level plus the answers anticipate the obvious follow-up
9: 8's level plus no answer needs a caveat he has to remember
10: 9's level plus the five answers are consistent with the applications he already filed

d2_landmines_absent_or_explained.instructions: Whether gaps, title oddities, level shifts or short tenures are absent or pre-explained
criteria: 0: a landmine is present and unexplained (a gap, a one-year stint, a title drop)
2: one landmine unexplained, one explained
3: all landmines present but explained only in a cover letter
4: one landmine explained inline, awkwardly
5: the obvious landmines are explained inline in one neutral clause each
6: 5's level plus explanations are factual, never defensive
7: 6's level plus no landmine invites a compensation or performance question
8: 7's level plus level changes are framed as scope growth
9: 8's level plus a screener would not pause on any line
10: 9's level plus the one apparent weakness is framed as a deliberate, explained choice

d3_level_scope_consistency.instructions: Whether seniority and scope hold steady or grow across roles
criteria: 0: a title or scope regression with no explanation
2: scope inconsistent between summary and role blocks
3: scope stated once globally and contradicted by roles
4: scope mostly consistent, one role unstated
5: scope stated per role and coherent
6: 5's level plus scope grows across the career
7: 6's level plus team size or budget trajectory is visible
8: 7's level plus the most recent role is the largest
9: 8's level plus the growth is evidenced, not asserted
10: 9's level plus a reader would describe him as one level throughout with growth inside it

d4_recent_role_relevant.instructions: Whether the most recent work obviously points at the target, or the bridge is stated
criteria: 0: the most recent role looks unrelated to the target
2: relevance implied but not stated
3: relevance stated in the summary only
4: relevance stated in the summary and one role line
5: the most recent role or an explicit bridge line makes relevance obvious
6: 5's level plus the bridge names the target's domain
7: 6's level plus the bridge carries an outcome
8: 7's level plus the bridge explains why he is moving now
9: 8's level plus the bridge is in the top third
10: 9's level plus the reader concludes he has already been doing this job

d5_no_invited_trap_question.instructions: Whether nothing in the resume invites a question he would rather not take on a first call
criteria: 0: a claim invites a trap question (comp history, reason for leaving, an overlapping employer)
2: one trap invited and unaddressed
3: a phrasing invites an ownership question he cannot evidence
4: a phrasing invites a scope question he cannot evidence
5: no phrase invites a question he cannot answer comfortably
6: 5's level plus nothing implies availability problems or short tenure ahead
7: 6's level plus nothing oversells a title he did not hold
8: 7's level plus nothing implies a client relationship that is really a prospect
9: 8's level plus a sceptic finds nothing to push on
10: 9's level plus every likely hard question has a prepared, true answer in the story bank

e1_skills_to_musthave_map.instructions: Whether each stated requirement maps to one line of evidence
criteria: 0: no mapping and no evidence
2: a skills list plus scattered evidence
3: half the must-haves have a matching evidence line
4: most have a matching line, the map is implicit
5: every must-have has a matching evidence line a reader can find
6: 5's level plus the mapping is visible in the bullet wording
7: 6's level plus the mapping is ordered like the posting
8: 7's level plus the top three requirements get the strongest evidence
9: 8's level plus the map is implicit but unmistakable
10: 9's level plus a screener could tick every box without re-reading

e2_gaps_named_not_hidden.instructions: Whether missing requirements are named honestly with the honest mitigation in the same breath
criteria: 0: gaps hidden or denied
2: gaps admitted without mitigation
3: gaps named vaguely
4: one gap named with weak mitigation
5: the real gaps are named with an honest mitigation each
6: 5's level plus the mitigation is adjacent experience, not a promise
7: 6's level plus no mitigation claims an unproven skill
8: 7's level plus the gaps are limited to nice-to-haves
9: 8's level plus he names what he would learn first
10: 9'slevel plus the gap handling itself demonstrates judgement

e3_one_sentence_why_this_company.instructions: Whether one sentence says why this company and not another, grounded in an observed fact
criteria: 0: generic or absent
2: about their size or funding, generic
3: names them but with a cliché
4: names them and one true fact, weakly connected
5: names them and one observed fact, connected to his work
6: 5's level plus the fact is not on their homepage
7: 6's level plus the sentence shows he read their product or customers
8: 7's level plus it names a problem he has already solved
9: 8's level plus it is one sentence he could say aloud
10: 9's level plus the sentence could open the interview

e4_language_match_to_posting.instructions: How closely the opening restates the posting's own top requirement and answers it
criteria: 0: no overlap in language
2: a few shared nouns, no structure
3: shared nouns and one shared duty
4: the top duty is implied, not stated
5: the top duty is restated and answered once
6: 5's level plus the second duty is answered
7: 6's level plus the top three duties each answered
8: 7's level plus the posting's phrasing is reused naturally
9: 8's level plus the opener reads as written for this job
10: 9'slevel plus every requirement is answered in the posting's own vocabulary

e5_lane_fit.instructions: Whether this is squarely his lane rather than a screening-out lane
criteria: 0: a known screen-out lane (coding-first IC, ML or research, security or platform architecture, quota sales)
2: one lane signal conflicts with the target
3: ambiguous lane, competes with specialists
4: adjacent lane with a credible bridge
5: AI strategy, transformation, adoption, implementation or customer-facing deployment, stated once
6: 5's level plus the resume does not signal a competing lane
7: 6's level plus the lane is named in the headline
8: 7'slevel plus the lane is evidenced by two roles
9: 8's level plus the lane is reinforced by scope, not title alone
10: 9's level plus a screener would describe him by the target's own lane name

rules.reason: the resume would not survive a five-question screen: fix the answerable-evidence gap before applying
a screen landmine (gap, title oddity, level shift) is unexplained
an ATS would mangle this file; fix layout before upload
must-haves missing in the target's own words; re-tailor
this is a screen-out lane for this candidate

notes: Category D is Phone-screen survival (Mike's choice, replacing Evidence/claim integrity on 2026-09-22). Deterministic claim and hash binding still runs in the pipeline, just not as a Jev question. 9.5 is the operating target the daily routine reports against; it is a goal, not a calibrated threshold. All verdicts are advisory because calibrated:false. Unrelated to the existing resume.ats pack, which keeps its own 4-level scale and thresholds: do NOT merge them or rescale them, because resume.ats rules read thresholds like 'score < 1.50' that mean something different on an 11-level scale. SCALE CORRECTION 2026-09-22: the live Jev API hard-caps score levels at 10 ("Too many score levels. Must have at most 10 levels"), contradicting the typesafe-jev skill doc which claims max 11. This pack therefore carries 10 levels labelled 0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10: the single "just above 0" filler rung was removed and every anchor label and body kept verbatim, so 0 = bad, 5 = average and 10 = world class still hold and rule thresholds (5.0) are unchanged. Operating goal is 9.5 on the 0-10 label scale. If the returned mean proves index-based (max 8 over 10 rungs) rather than label-based, the equivalent goal is 8.55 and the next run must say so rather than rescale silently.
